Surface: infra

## Current State

`toIssuePayload` (`plugin/bin/lib/docs-health/issue-payload.js`) renders the header line as `**Doc:** ${finding.target} | **Section:** … | **Category:** … | **Misleads:** … | **Classification:** …` and the title as `Doc {category}: ${finding.target} — ${finding.section}`, where `finding.target` is the registry doc id: `scope.js` walks `docs/**` and sets `id` to the path relative to `docs/` with the `.md` extension stripped (`{ kind: 'doc', id, path }`, `path` being the absolute file path). The judge template writes `"target": "{target.id}"` into every finding, `validate-finding.js` requires `target` as a string, and the fingerprint basis is `['assetType', 'target', 'section', 'description']` (`fingerprint.js`), so `target` must stay the id for dedup and for the `--target <id>` round-trip. Nothing in the filed body states the repo-relative path; `flow/materialize.md`'s "Named-location drift (#315)" then tells every builder to treat `plans/2026-08-30-…-ledger` as a hypothesis and grep for it, on a location the filer itself mis-stated.

Observed on plugin 6.114.1 across two consecutive dispatch builds in a downstream project: each build located the doc by grepping for the stale hash and logged the `plans/` → `docs/plans/` mismatch as a ledger observation. This repository's own open docs-health records carry the same shape in their titles (`Doc staleness: plans/…-ledger — Freshness`).

The id → path mapping is a pure function (`docs/{id}.md`), so no new finding field or CLI output is needed to render a resolvable location. `tests/bin-lib/docs-health/issue-payload.test.js` pins that the body starts with `**Doc:**` and carries the fingerprint marker.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Resolvable location in the body and title, id kept for identity.** In `toIssuePayload`, derive `docPath = docs/${finding.target}.md` and render the header as `**Doc:** {docPath} | **Id:** {finding.target} | **Section:** … | …` (the remaining fields unchanged) and the title as `Doc {category}: {docPath} — {section}`. `finding.target`, the fingerprint basis, `payload.target`, and the marker stay byte-identical, so existing records still dedup against new findings for the same doc and section.
- [ ] **Nested-docs correctness.** For an id containing directory segments (`plans/2026-…`), `docPath` is `docs/plans/2026-….md`; for a `--dir <path>` audit that walks a root other than `docs/`, use that root as the prefix (`scope.js` exposes it, or thread the resolved `docsRoot` alongside `verifiedAsOf`), never a hardcoded `docs/`.
- [ ] **Prose.** `skills/docs-health/SKILL.md` Step 6 (filing) gains one sentence: the body's `Doc:` field is the repo-relative path and `Id:` is the registry id `--target` accepts. `flow/materialize.md`'s Named-location drift paragraph gains a clause: a `by:docs-health` record's `Doc:` path is resolvable as written and needs only an `ls`, not a grep.
- [ ] **Tests.** `issue-payload.test.js`: the header starts with `**Doc:** docs/{id}.md` and carries `**Id:** {id}`; the title uses the path; `payload.target` and the fingerprint are unchanged for the same input (assert equality against a fixture computed before the change); a nested id renders `docs/plans/….md`; a non-default docs root renders under that root. A prose pin for the two sentences.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For a finding with `target: 'plans/2026-08-30-x-ledger'`, `toIssuePayload` renders a body starting with `**Doc:** docs/plans/2026-08-30-x-ledger.md | **Id:** plans/2026-08-30-x-ledger |` and a title `Doc {category}: docs/plans/2026-08-30-x-ledger.md — {section}`.
2. `payload.target`, `payload.fingerprint`, and `extractFingerprint(payload.body)` are identical before and after the change for the same finding, pinned by a test.
3. Filing the same finding twice still dedups (the existing dedup path keyed on the fingerprint marker is unchanged, covered by the existing dedup tests).
4. `SKILL.md` Step 6 and `materialize.md` carry the sentences above once each.
5. `npm test` green; every existing case in `tests/bin-lib/docs-health/` passes with only the two header/title assertions updated.

## Technical Approach

Render, don't re-key: the id remains the identity everywhere (fingerprint, `--target`, `payload.target`), and only the human-facing header and title change to the resolvable path. Compute the path in the payload composer from the id and the docs root rather than adding a `path` field to the finding schema, so the judge template and `validate-finding.js` are untouched. Records already filed keep their old text; nothing rewrites them.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/docs-health/issue-payload.js` — `docPath` derivation; header `Doc:`/`Id:` fields; title
- `plugin/bin/docs-health.js` — thread the resolved docs root into `toIssuePayload` only if `--dir` audits need a non-`docs/` prefix
- `plugin/skills/docs-health/SKILL.md` — Step 6 sentence
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — Named-location drift clause
- `tests/bin-lib/docs-health/issue-payload.test.js` — updated header/title assertions; identity-stability, nested-id, and docs-root cases

## Gotchas

- The `**Doc:**` prefix is pinned by an existing test ("body starts directly with the header line"); keep the field first so that assertion needs only its expected value changed.
- `harness-health`, `code-health`, and `journey-health` payloads have their own header conventions; this change is docs-health only.
- Titles are not a dedup key (dedup is fingerprint-marker based), so the title change cannot re-file already-tracked findings; state that in the PR description with the dedup test named.
- A `--target <id>` invocation still accepts the id; do not accept the path there, or the round-trip contract in `SKILL.md`'s CLI section changes.

## Original request

**Summary:** `/claude-tweaks:docs-health` files its records with `**Doc:** {target}` where `{target}` is the sweep's doc id — "the doc's path relative to `docs/`, without the `.md` extension" (the same id `--target <id>` accepts). The record's title reuses it. A reader or builder who takes the record at its word (`plans/2026-08-30-spec-253-254-255-digest-full-page-ledger`) looks for a top-level `plans/` directory that does not exist; the file is `docs/plans/2026-08-30-spec-253-254-255-digest-full-page-ledger.md`. Every docs-health record therefore ships with a named location that `flow/materialize.md`'s "Named-location drift" note (#315) tells the builder to treat as a hypothesis and grep for — drift that the filer itself introduces, on every record, rather than drift that a later refactor caused.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `bin/lib/docs-health/issue-payload.js` (the `**Doc:** ${finding.target} | **Section:** …` kind line and the derived title), i.e. `/claude-tweaks:docs-health` Step 6's filing payload; the same id also drives the record's `docshealth-*` fingerprint, so any change must keep the fingerprint basis stable.

**Use case:** Two consecutive dispatch-driven builds of docs-health records against a downstream project (records for `plans/2026-08-31-finish-rebrand-repo-folder-rename-ledger` and `plans/2026-08-30-spec-253-254-255-digest-full-page-ledger`) each had to locate the target by grepping for the stale hash the record described, then log the `plans/` → `docs/plans/` mismatch as a build-ledger observation. The upstream repository's own docs-health backlog shows the same shape (`Doc staleness: plans/2026-08-25-record-1424-ledger — Freshness`, etc.), so this is the filer's convention, not a downstream configuration.

**Suggested remedy:** Keep the doc id for the fingerprint and the `--target` round-trip, but make the record body state a resolvable location — e.g. `**Doc:** docs/plans/…-ledger.md` (repo-relative, from `next-target`'s `path` field, which the CLI already returns alongside `id`) with the bare id retained in a separate `**Id:**` field or the fingerprint comment. Alternatively keep `Doc:` as the id but add a `**Path:** {repo-relative}` field beside it, so `materialize.md`'s named-location verification has a path to `ls` instead of a grep target to infer.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

---

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`toIssuePayload` (`plugin/bin/lib/harness-health/issue-payload.js`) composes every harness-health `patch` finding's Deliverables as two fenced blocks, `**Current:**` (`finding.oldString`) and `**Proposed:**` (`finding.newString`), plus a header line naming asset, section, category (`drift` | `template-conformance` | `best-practice`), classification, and confidence; `specShapedBody` adds the `Verified-as-of: {sha}` stamp. For CLAUDE.md and rules, dimensions 7 and 8 of `_shared/harness-health-analysis.md` judge against the live origin template (`skills/init/claude-md-template.md`, `skills/init/rules-template.md`), and `judge-procedure.md`'s finding schema carries no field naming which template the Proposed text came from or which plugin version rendered it. The body therefore reads as "replace Current with Proposed", and nothing in `flow/materialize.md` or `build/SKILL.md` distinguishes a `by:harness-health` record's Proposed block from authored deliverable text.

Observed on plugin 6.114.1: a Philosophy "No implicit deferrals" drift record filed against the 6.111.0 template was built after the template line had changed wording; the planner re-read the installed template on its own initiative and the whole-branch review confirmed the committed line byte-identical to it. Neither step was required by the record or by `/build`; a builder applying the Proposed block literally would have shipped text the next sweep re-files.

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` already reads the running plugin's version from `{pluginRoot}/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; `bin/harness-health.js` resolves `verifiedAsOf` once per run and threads it into `toIssuePayload`. `materialize.js` already parses one body-metadata stamp (`Verified-as-of`) into an envelope field (`drift`) with a stderr sentence on staleness.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Name the template and its version at filing.** `judge-procedure.md`'s finding schema gains an optional `templateSource` (repo-relative path of the origin template the Proposed text was derived from), set by the judge for every `claude-md`/`rule` finding in the `template-conformance` and `best-practice` categories. `bin/harness-health.js` reads the running plugin's version once per run (the same `{CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` read `session-start.js` performs; `manifest-path.js` is for historical git refs, not the running build) and threads `pluginVersion` into `toIssuePayload` beside `verifiedAsOf`. When `finding.templateSource` is set, the body carries a metadata line `Template: {templateSource} @ {pluginVersion}` (same convention as `Verified-as-of`) and the Deliverables open with one sentence: the Proposed block is a snapshot of that template at that version; at build time re-derive the replacement from the installed template and treat the fence as the intended shape, not the bytes.
- [ ] **Materialize surfaces the version delta.** `record.js`: `extractTemplateStamp(body)` beside `extractVerifiedAsOf`. `materialize.js`: when present, read the installed plugin version (the same `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` read) and add `template: { path, recorded, installed, changed }` to the envelope; when `changed`, print one stderr sentence in the drift sentence's shape ("Proposed block was rendered from {path} at {recorded}; installed is {installed} — re-derive from the installed template before implementing"). Absent line → `template: null`, byte-identical behavior.
- [ ] **Build names the re-read.** `flow/materialize.md` gains a "Template snapshot" paragraph beside the drift paragraphs; `build/SKILL.md`'s writing-plans handoff adds: when `template.changed`, the plan's first task re-reads `{path}` at the installed version and derives the replacement from it, and the PR description quotes the installed template line the commit matches.
- [ ] **Tests.** `tests/bin-lib/harness-health/issue-payload.test.js`: `Template:` line and the snapshot sentence present for a `template-conformance` claude-md finding with `templateSource`, absent for a `drift` skill finding, absent when `pluginVersion` is not supplied. A sibling of `tests/materialize-drift.test.js` for the `template` envelope field and stderr sentence (recorded ≠ installed, recorded = installed, no line, unreadable manifest degrades to `null`). Prose pins for `judge-procedure.md`'s schema field, `materialize.md`'s paragraph, and `build/SKILL.md`'s handoff bullet.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A harness-health CLAUDE.md `template-conformance` finding files a record whose body carries `Template: skills/init/claude-md-template.md @ {version}` and the snapshot sentence above the Current/Proposed fences; a skill `drift` finding's body is byte-identical to today's.
2. `node bin/materialize.js #N` on such a record reports `template.changed: true` and prints the stderr sentence when the installed version differs, `changed: false` and no sentence when equal, and `template: null` for a record without the line.
3. `build/SKILL.md` and `flow/materialize.md` state the re-derive rule once each; `judge-procedure.md` documents `templateSource`.
4. Replaying the reported case in a fixture (record stamped at an older version, installed template line reworded) yields a plan whose first task names the installed template read; quoted in the PR description.
5. `npm test` green; every existing case in `tests/bin-lib/harness-health/` and `tests/materialize-drift.test.js` passes unchanged.

## Technical Approach

Same shape as the `Verified-as-of` stamp: one optional body-metadata line written by the filer, one optional envelope field read by materialize, one prose consumer in build. Version, not sha, is the right key here — the template ships inside the plugin, so the installed plugin version is what the builder can compare against without a checkout of this repo. Do not rewrite already-filed records; only new filings carry the line.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/harness-health/issue-payload.js` — `Template:` line + snapshot sentence when `templateSource` is set; `pluginVersion` param
- `plugin/bin/harness-health.js` — read the running build's version once from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; thread it
- `plugin/skills/harness-health/judge-procedure.md` — `templateSource` in the finding schema
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record.js` — `extractTemplateStamp`
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js` — `template` envelope field + stderr sentence
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — "Template snapshot" paragraph
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — writing-plans handoff bullet
- `tests/bin-lib/harness-health/issue-payload.test.js`, `tests/materialize-template-stamp.test.js` — new cases and pins

## Gotchas

- The running plugin's version is the installed build's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` under `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, not this repo's `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, which is ahead of the installed build during development; the sweep and materialize must both read the running manifest.
- `specShapedBody` renders metadata lines before the first `##`; keep `Template:` single-line and plain, never YAML.
- `docs-health`/`code-health`/`journey-health` payloads share the `verifiedAsOf` shape but have no origin template; do not add the line there.
- A `best-practice` finding may cite guidance rather than a template line; `templateSource` is optional, and the line is emitted only when the judge set it.

## Original request

**Summary:** A harness-health CLAUDE.md drift record quotes the template's replacement text as of the plugin version installed when it was filed; by build time a newer plugin can carry different wording, so applying the record's Proposed block literally closes one drift and opens another that the next sweep re-files.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` (drift-record body for template-derived CLAUDE.md sections) and `/claude-tweaks:build`'s handling of `by:harness-health` records

**Use case:** A drift record for the Philosophy "No implicit deferrals" bullet was filed against the v6.111.0 template and built under v6.114.1, whose `skills/init/claude-md-template.md` line 154 had changed wording in the meantime (same mechanism, more precise phrasing). The record's body reads as a plain "replace Current with Proposed" instruction. The build only avoided re-introducing drift because the planner independently re-read the installed template and its whole-branch review confirmed the committed line byte-identical to that template — neither step was required by the record or by `/build`. A builder that trusted the Proposed block (the natural reading) would have shipped text the harness-health conformance sweep immediately flags again.

**Suggested remedy (either or both):** (a) harness-health drift records for template-derived sections state the template version the Proposed block was snapshotted from and instruct the builder to re-derive the replacement from the *installed* template at build time; (b) `/build`'s materialize step, for `by:harness-health` records carrying `Verified-as-of`, compares the record's plugin version against the installed one and notes a version delta in the plan so the re-read is a named step rather than a planner's initiative.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Three checkers implement `_shared/work-record.md`'s spec-shaped-body rule "no unresolved placeholder markers (the two deferral tokens and the ambiguity HTML-comment marker) outside the verbatim `## Original request` section", and none of them distinguishes a marker in authored prose from one inside quoted code:

- `shapeGate` (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js`): `PLACEHOLDER_RE = /\bTBD\b|\bTODO\b|<!--\s*ambiguity:/` tested against everything before `## Original request` (#1240). This is `/flow`'s materialization hard gate; a hit exits `materialize.js` with `unresolved-placeholder` and Settling points at `/claude-tweaks:specify`.
- `validateShaped` (`plugin/bin/lib/compose-record/compose.js`): a substring loop over `PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS` with the same section exemption, used at compose time.
- The prose rule itself (`_shared/work-record.md`, the spec-shaped-body list), re-run by `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine`'s Step 3.5 body-shape auto-downgrade and the grant gate; `specify/shaping-mode.md` therefore tells shapers never to *mention* the tokens, even in prose.

Harness-health drift records quote the current and proposed CLAUDE.md text verbatim in fenced blocks under `## Deliverables` by construction. When the quoted bullet is the "No implicit deferrals" philosophy line (which ends "…leave a T-O-D-O comment without a corresponding record"), every such record fails the gate although nothing in it is unresolved: observed on plugin 6.114.1, `materialize.js` exit 1 `unresolved-placeholder`, worked around by a logged hand materialization. The same shape recurs for any CLAUDE.md section whose template wording contains the word, and for any record that quotes code or prose containing it.

Tests: `tests/bin-lib/issues/materialize-format.test.js` (`shapeGate` cases including the #1240 exemption and "a genuine marker in an authored section still fails"); `tests/bin-lib/compose-record/` for `validateShaped`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **One helper, two checkers.** Add `stripCodeSpans(text)` to `plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js` (exported): removes fenced blocks (```` ``` ```` and `~~~`, any info string, unclosed fence runs to end of text) and inline code spans (backtick runs of any length, per CommonMark) from the authored text before `PLACEHOLDER_RE` is applied. `validateShaped` in `compose.js` imports and applies the same helper before its marker loop. A bare marker in authored prose still fails in both.
- [ ] **Prose rule and shaping guidance.** `_shared/work-record.md`'s spec-shaped-body bullet gains the clause "or inside a fenced code block / inline code span, which quotes content rather than authoring it". `specify/shaping-mode.md`'s authoring-constraint paragraph is narrowed the same way: a token inside backticks is permitted (it is what the two JS checkers now skip); a prose mention remains forbidden. `refine`'s Step 3.5 and the grant gate cite the rule by reference, so they need no text change; confirm with a grep and edit only if either restates the token list.
- [ ] **Tests.** `materialize-format.test.js`: a Deliverables fence quoting a line with `T-O-D-O` passes; an inline-code `` `T-O-D-O` `` passes; a bare `T-O-D-O` in the same section still fails; an unclosed fence containing the marker passes (fence runs to end of authored text); a marker after a closed fence still fails. Sibling cases in the `validateShaped` suite. The `materialize` CLI case "an unshaped record fails the gate" stays as is.
- [ ] `flow/materialize.md`'s "Materialization hard gate" sentence names the code-span exemption in the same breath as the `## Original request` one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `shapeGate(body)` returns `{ ok: true }` for a body whose only `T-O-D-O`/`T-B-D` occurrences are inside fenced blocks or inline code spans in authored sections, and `{ ok: false, missing: ['unresolved-placeholder'] }` when a bare marker appears in authored prose in the same body.
2. `validateShaped` agrees with `shapeGate` on every fixture in both suites (a shared fixture module or duplicated literals, either way asserted equal).
3. Every existing case in `materialize-format.test.js` and the `validateShaped` suite passes unchanged, including "a genuine marker in an authored section still fails when an Original request section is also present".
4. `_shared/work-record.md`, `specify/shaping-mode.md`, and `flow/materialize.md` state the exemption once each, and a grep for the token list under `plugin/skills/backlog` shows no third restatement of the token rule.
5. The reported record shape (harness-health drift record quoting the "No implicit deferrals" bullet) materializes with exit 0 in a fixture; quoted in the PR description.
6. `npm test` green.

## Technical Approach

Strip, don't special-case: removing code spans before the regex keeps `PLACEHOLDER_RE` and `PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS` untouched and the exemption identical in both checkers. Handle the unclosed-fence case by treating the run to end-of-text as code (the safer direction: a truncated fence is quoted content, not authored prose). Apply the helper *after* the `## Original request` cut, so the two exemptions compose without interaction.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js` — `stripCodeSpans`; apply in `shapeGate`; export
- `plugin/bin/lib/compose-record/compose.js` — apply in `validateShaped`
- `plugin/skills/_shared/work-record.md` — spec-shaped-body bullet clause
- `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md` — narrowed authoring constraint
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — hard-gate sentence
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/materialize-format.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/compose-record/*.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- An inline-code span cannot contain its own delimiter run; match backtick runs by length (`` `+ `` opening, same length closing) or a single-backtick `T-O-D-O` inside a double-backtick span is mis-cut.
- `sectionText` and the section-presence checks run on the *unstripped* body; only the placeholder scan sees the stripped text, so a section whose only content is a fenced block still counts as non-empty.
- `_shared/work-record.md`'s rule is also quoted by `capture/SKILL.md`'s born-ready branch; a grep for the token list decides whether that quote needs the clause too (AC 4's sweep).
- The exemption widens the gate; keep the "bare marker after a closed fence still fails" case so a stray `T-O-D-O` cannot hide behind an earlier code block.

## Original request

**Summary:** `shapeGate`'s placeholder scan (`\bTODO\b`) rejects a fully-shaped harness-health drift record because its authored Deliverables section quotes the CLAUDE.md bullet being replaced, and that bullet's own wording says "leave a TODO comment" — the marker is the deliverable, not a placeholder.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js` (`shapeGate` / `PLACEHOLDER_RE`) — `/flow`'s materialization hard gate

**Repro steps:**
1. Run `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` against a project whose CLAUDE.md Philosophy section carries the pre-#621 "No implicit deferrals" bullet (the one ending "…leave a TODO comment without a corresponding record").
2. Let it file its drift record: the body's `## Deliverables` section contains two fenced blocks — **Current** (the stale bullet, verbatim) and **Proposed** (the template bullet, verbatim); both contain the words "TODO comment". All three required sections are present and non-empty; no `TBD`, no `<!-- ambiguity:` marker anywhere.
3. Dispatch it: `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR=… /claude-tweaks:flow #{n}` → `bin/materialize.js {n} --run-dir …` exits 1 with `unresolved-placeholder`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the record passes the gate — the marker word occurs only inside fenced code that quotes the exact text the deliverable replaces, in an authored section; nothing is unresolved.
Actual: `unresolved-placeholder`, exit 1. The build had to override with a logged composer-based materialization (`materialize-format.js`'s own `composeHeader`/`composeFile`) because Settling would point at `/specify`, which cannot remove the word from a correct deliverable. #1240 (closed) and #1633 (open) exempt only the verbatim `## Original request` section, so neither covers a marker inside a fenced/inline code span in an authored section.

**Suggested remedy:** strip fenced code blocks and inline code spans from the authored text before applying `PLACEHOLDER_RE` (a quoted line of text is content, not a placeholder), keep failing on a bare marker in authored prose, and add a regression case whose Deliverables fence quotes a line containing the marker word. Harness-health drift records quote Current/Proposed text by construction, so this shape recurs for every CLAUDE.md section whose template wording mentions TODO.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/verify.js` classifies each check's output with `sniffFamily` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/extract.js`) and parses counts with `parseCounts(text, family)`. Two facts make vitest output unparseable today, and only one of them is the ANSI colour the report names:

1. **The counts path never strips ANSI.** `stripAnsi` exists in `extract.js` (added for #1925's `extractFailingFiles`, whose comment cites this record as the lesson) but is applied only inside `extractFailingFiles`; `sniffFamily`, `parseCounts`, `summaryLine`, and `extractFailingRegion` run on the raw text. A coloured ` FAIL ` or `Tests` line is invisible to the `^FAIL `/`^Tests:` anchors.
2. **Vitest's summary shape is not a recognized family.** `SUMMARY_MARKERS` are jest (`^Tests:.*failed`, `^PASS `/`^FAIL `) and pytest (`^=+ .*(passed|failed).*=+$`); `parseCounts`'s `summary` branch reads only `^Tests:.*$` (colon) or the pytest banner. Vitest prints `Test Files  64 passed (64)` and `Tests  727 passed (727)` — no colon, a `(total)` suffix — so even colour-free vitest output sniffs as `generic` and returns `counts: null`.

`counts: null` is then silent by design at every layer: `report.js` omits the `counts` key (pinned by "counts is omitted from the entry when null"), `verify.js` sets `testCountRegression = null` when `counts.tests` is not a number, and the stdout render prints the CAVEAT line only when a regression object exists. `test/verification.md`'s "Suite-count regression caveat (#881)" section describes the comparison without naming the unparsed case. Neither `run.js` nor `verify.js` sets `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` on the child.

Observed on plugin 6.114.1 (Windows host, pnpm + Vitest 2.x, colour on without a TTY): `counts: null` on both a 64-file and a 43-file suite across two runs, `testCountRegression: null`, while `tests.log` carried both vitest summary lines under escape codes.

Tests: `tests/bin-lib/verify/extract.test.js` (jest and pytest count fixtures; an ANSI case only for `extractFailingFiles`), `report.test.js`, `count-stamp.test.js`, `cli.test.js`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Strip ANSI once, before every parser.** In `verify.js`'s check-result composition (the block that calls `sniffFamily`/`summaryLine`/`extractFailingRegion`/`parseCounts`), pass `stripAnsi(text)` to all four; export `stripAnsi` from `extract.js` if it is not already. `extractFailingFiles` keeps its own call (idempotent). The raw log file stays raw.
- [ ] **Recognize vitest.** Add a vitest marker to `SUMMARY_MARKERS` (`^\s*Test Files\s+\d+ (?:passed|failed)` or `^\s*Tests\s+\d+ (?:passed|failed)`) and a vitest branch in `parseCounts`'s `summary` family that reads the `Tests` line: `(\d+) passed`, `(\d+) failed`, `(\d+) skipped`, and the `\((\d+)\)` total, using the same known-category guard as the jest path (an unknown `(\d+) word` phrase blocks derivation rather than guessing). `Test Files` is never used for `counts.tests`; the `Tests` line is.
- [ ] **Belt and braces on colour.** `run.js` spawns the child with `NO_COLOR=1` and `FORCE_COLOR=0` merged into `process.env` (caller values win if already set), so well-behaved runners emit plain text; stripping stays authoritative for runners that ignore both.
- [ ] **Never disable the comparison silently.** When a `tests` check ran, a count stamp is in play, and `counts` parsed `null`, the report entry gains `countsUnparsed: { family }` and the stdout render prints one line in the CAVEAT shape: `CAVEAT: tests counts unparsed (family {family}) — count-stamp comparison skipped; see {logPath}`. `report.testCountRegression` stays `null`. `test/verification.md`'s "Suite-count regression caveat" section gains one sentence naming this line.
- [ ] **Tests.** `extract.test.js`: vitest fixture (coloured and plain) sniffs `summary` and parses `{tests: 727, pass: 727, fail: 0}`; a vitest line with `| 3 failed` parses `fail: 3`; a jest fixture wrapped in ANSI still parses. `report.test.js`: `countsUnparsed` present when set, omitted otherwise. `cli.test.js`: stdout carries the new CAVEAT line for an unparseable `tests` check under `--count-stamp`, and not when counts parse. `run.test.js`: child env carries `NO_COLOR=1`/`FORCE_COLOR=0` without overriding caller-set values.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `parseCounts(stripAnsi(VITEST_COLOURED), sniffFamily(stripAnsi(VITEST_COLOURED)))` returns `{tests: 727, pass: 727, fail: 0}` for the reported output shape; the plain-text equivalent returns the same.
2. Existing jest, pytest, and TAP count fixtures return byte-identical results; the "never a guess" null cases stay null.
3. `node bin/verify.js --count-stamp {p} --cmd tests="{vitest cmd}"` run twice records `checks.tests.counts.tests` both times and prints the drop CAVEAT when the second run's count is lower (fixture-driven in `cli.test.js`).
4. An unparseable `tests` check under a count stamp prints the `CAVEAT: tests counts unparsed` line and sets `countsUnparsed` in `report.json`; no line appears when counts parse or when no stamp is in play.
5. The child process env includes `NO_COLOR=1` and `FORCE_COLOR=0` unless the caller set either.
6. `npm test` green; every existing case in `tests/bin-lib/verify/*` passes unchanged.

## Technical Approach

Strip at the boundary, once, so no parser needs to know about colour; add the vitest shape as a third summary dialect beside jest and pytest rather than loosening the jest regex (a colon-less `Tests` line must not be confused with a TAP `# tests` block — TAP precedence in `sniffFamily` is pinned). Keep counts fail-toward-absence (#892's rule): the new caveat line makes absence visible; it never fabricates a number.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/extract.js` — vitest marker + `parseCounts` branch; export `stripAnsi`
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — strip before the four parsers; `countsUnparsed`; render the caveat line
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js` — child env `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js` — carry `countsUnparsed` into the entry
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — one sentence under "Suite-count regression caveat (#881)"
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/extract.test.js`, `report.test.js`, `cli.test.js`, `run.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- `ANSI_RE` is ESC-anchored on purpose (a literal `[1m` in test output is not a code); keep it, do not widen to bare bracket sequences.
- Vitest prints `Tests` once but `Test Files` too; only the `Tests` line feeds `counts.tests`, or a 64-file suite would be recorded as 64 tests and the drop detector would fire on the wrong axis.
- `count-stamp.js`'s regression compares `previous.tests` to `current.tests` only; the vitest branch must fill `tests` from the parenthesized total when present, else `pass + fail`, matching the jest path's convention.
- Some CI images honour `FORCE_COLOR=1` from the runner's own config over `NO_COLOR`; that is why stripping, not the env, is the fix the acceptance criteria test.

## Original request

**Summary:** `bin/verify.js` records `counts: null` for a `tests` check whose output is vitest's default colour-coded summary (`Tests  64 passed (64)` wrapped in ANSI escape sequences), which silently disables the `--count-stamp` regression comparison the runner documents.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/verify.js` (the `tests` summary parser; `_shared`/`test/verification.md`'s "Suite-count regression caveat")

**Repro steps:**
1. In a project whose test command is Vitest (^2.x) with default reporter and colour on (a normal TTY-less `pnpm test` still emits ANSI colour codes on this Windows host), run `node bin/verify.js --count-stamp <path> --cmd tests="pnpm --filter <pkg> test"` twice.
2. Read `report.json` after each run.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: `checks.tests.counts.tests` holds the parsed total (64 test files / N tests here), and the second run compares it against the stamp so a drop would print the documented `CAVEAT:` line.
Actual: `checks.tests.counts` is `null` on both runs (observed twice in one session, on both a core suite of 64 files and a web suite of 43 files), `testCountRegression` is `null`, and no caveat could ever fire — while the raw `tests.log` plainly contains `Test Files  64 passed (64)` / `Tests  727 passed (727)` once ANSI sequences are stripped. The parser appears to match the summary line only when it is free of escape codes.

Suggested fix: strip `\x1b\[[0-9;]*m` before applying the summary regexes (or run the child with `NO_COLOR=1`/`FORCE_COLOR=0` in its env), and surface `counts: null` on a `tests` check as its own visible line rather than silently disabling the comparison.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

Surface: backend

## Current State

Record #649 added `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s fan-out single-assistant-message-rule
sentence and per-site citations (AC1, fully test-pinned in `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js`,
18/18 passing). AC2 — "A `/specify` red-team over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues launches its
personas in ≤ (number of sub-issues) assistant messages, verified in the transcript by `Agent`
tool_use blocks sharing a message id" — is a live-behavior criterion that cannot be verified by a
static `node --test` assertion; it can only be confirmed by observing an actual future `/specify`
decomposition run's transcript.

## Deliverables

Confirm, at the next `/specify` decomposition run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues, that
persona dispatch actually batches into ≤N assistant messages per `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s
fan-out single-assistant-message rule and `red-team.md`'s per-sub-issue batching unit. Record the
observation (transcript excerpt or note) against this item, or file a defect against
`red-team.md`'s dispatch prose if it does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

A `/specify` run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues is observed; its persona `Agent` tool_use
calls are confirmed (via transcript `tool_use` block message-id grouping) to arrive in ≤ (number of
sub-issues) assistant messages.

## Technical Approach

Wait for (or trigger) a `/claude-tweaks:specify` decomposition-mode run that produces 2 or more

Surface: infra

## Current State

`_shared/dev-url-detection.md` resolves (or starts) a per-worktree dev server and sets
`APP_URL = http://localhost:{port}` (an ephemeral, worktree-isolated port — see its Step 2.7
Worktree Awareness gate). `skills/test/qa-prompts.md`'s Phase 3 dispatch template fills
`{story.url}` verbatim into each dispatched qa-agent's prompt (lines ~76 and ~139: `**URL:**
{story.url}`) — there is no rewrite step anywhere between resolving `APP_URL` and composing that
prompt. A story file that pins an absolute origin (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...`) therefore
drives whatever server is actually listening on that literal port — the main checkout's server on
the live database — even when `dev-url-detection.md` correctly resolved a different, isolated
`APP_URL` for this worktree run. This is exactly the wrong-code/wrong-data failure Step 2.7's
worktree-awareness gate exists to prevent, except it happens one layer downstream, after
`APP_URL` has already been correctly resolved.

Confirmed on a real run (plugin 6.118.0): four story files pinned absolute origins, two used
root-relative paths; every dispatched qa-agent for the four absolute-origin stories would have
navigated to the wrong server. The operator manually rewrote the origin in every dispatched
prompt by hand (~20 minutes of pre-flight) because the plugin has no documented convention for
whether story `url:` values should be absolute or `APP_URL`-relative, and no rewrite mechanism
either way.

## Deliverables

- At dispatch (`qa-prompts.md`'s Phase 3 template construction, wherever `{story.url}` is
  currently substituted verbatim), when a story's `url` carries an absolute origin
  (scheme+host+port) that differs from the resolved `APP_URL`'s origin, substitute `APP_URL`'s
  origin for the story's own origin, preserving the story's path/query/fragment unchanged.
- Log the rewrite once per run (not once per story) when at least one story needed it — naming
  the original and resolved origins — so a QA report makes clear the substitution happened.
- Document in `stories/SKILL.md` that a story's `url:` field should be a root-relative path
  joined to the resolved `APP_URL` at dispatch time — the convention this record's fix
  establishes — and that an absolute origin, if present, gets its origin rewritten to `APP_URL`'s
  rather than followed literally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A story with `url: http://127.0.0.1:9999/dashboard` dispatched under a resolved
  `APP_URL = http://localhost:54321` navigates to `http://localhost:54321/dashboard`, not the
  literal `9999` port.
- A story with a root-relative `url: /dashboard` is joined to `APP_URL` unchanged (no regression
  to the already-working case the record's own use case confirms works today).
- The rewrite is logged exactly once per QA run when triggered, not once per affected story.
- `stories/SKILL.md` documents the `url:` field convention (root-relative preferred; an absolute
  origin gets rewritten, not followed literally) where the story schema is otherwise documented.

## Technical Approach

Add the rewrite as a small pure function (parse the story's `url`, and when it carries a
scheme+host+port that differs from the resolved `APP_URL`'s own scheme+host+port, replace just
the origin, keeping path/query/fragment intact — a root-relative `url` needs no parsing branch at
all, since `new URL(story.url, APP_URL).toString()` already does the right thing for both shapes)
applied once, at the point in `qa-prompts.md`'s Phase 3 (or wherever the per-story dispatch prompt
is actually assembled, likely just before the `{story.url}` substitution at lines ~76/139) where
`APP_URL` is already in scope. Log the rewrite via this test pipeline's existing decision-log
convention if a run directory is active, otherwise to the QA report directly
(`qa-reporting.md`'s existing output conventions).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/test/qa-prompts.md` — apply the origin rewrite before substituting `{story.url}`
  into the Phase 3 dispatch template (~lines 76, 139)
- `plugin/skills/stories/SKILL.md` — document the `url:` field convention
- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — read-only reference: this is where `APP_URL` is
  resolved; not modified by this record

## Gotchas

- Do not silently swallow a story whose origin points at a genuinely different host on purpose
  (e.g. a story deliberately testing an external service, not the app under test) — the rewrite
  should only ever touch the origin, and if a project genuinely needs a story to hit a different
  host, that's outside this record's scope; flag it as a known limitation rather than trying to
  distinguish intent here.
- The log-once-per-run rule (not per-story) matters for QA report readability on a large story
  suite — don't regress it to log every rewritten story individually.

## Original request

**Summary:** `_shared/dev-url-detection.md` resolves (or starts) a per-worktree dev server on a free port, but `qa-procedures.md`'s dispatch passes each story's `url:` verbatim; a story written as `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` therefore drives the main checkout's server (wrong code, live database) even when `APP_URL` resolved to the ephemeral worktree port.
**Kind:** Gap
**Affected component:** `skills/test/qa-procedures.md` / `skills/test/qa-prompts.md` / `skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md`
**Use case:**
Pipeline QA inside a `/claude-tweaks:flow` worktree run (plugin 6.118.0) on a private project whose story files pin absolute origins (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` in four files, root-relative paths in two). `dev-url-detection.md` correctly started a dev server on an ephemeral port against a per-worktree test database. Following the procedure literally, every dispatched qa-agent would have navigated to the pinned port — the main checkout's server on the live database — which is exactly the wrong-code/wrong-data case the worktree-awareness step (2.7) warns about. The operator had to rewrite the origin in every dispatched prompt by hand (about 20 minutes of pre-flight before the first story could run), and the plugin offers no place to state the project's convention (absolute story URLs rewritten at dispatch vs. relative paths joined to `APP_URL`).
**Definition:** Clear — at dispatch, substitute the resolved `APP_URL` origin for a story's embedded absolute origin (scheme+host+port) when they differ, log the rewrite once per run, and document in `stories/SKILL.md` that story `url:` values should be root-relative paths joined to `APP_URL`.
**Plugin version:** 6.118.0

Surface: infra

## Current State
`bin/lib/wrap-up/state.js`'s `readState` derives push status from the configured upstream only: it runs `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`, and when that fails it sets `upstream: null` and `pushed: false` — the comment reads "Absent an upstream there is nowhere for the work to have gone, so it is unpushed". `bin/lib/wrap-up/render.js` then prints `{head} — {commits}, UNPUSHED (no upstream)`, and `bin/wrap-up-state.js` uses `state.upstream` to pick which reflog to read. That premise is false for every `pr-first` run: `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s Step 2 and `_shared/git-discipline.md`'s phase-exit push use `git push origin {branch}` with no `-u`, so `@{u}` stays unset (or, since #1860, points at the branch-off point `origin/main` when the worktree was created with `-b {branch} origin/main`) while `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` is up to date after every push. The State block that `wrap-up/summary-template.md` says to render verbatim therefore claims UNPUSHED for work that origin already holds, and the reporter had to run `git branch --set-upstream-to` by hand to get a truthful line.

The ref the helper needs is already local: `git push origin {branch}` updates `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` in the pushing checkout, so no fetch is required to judge a push this run made; a fetch would only matter for pushes made elsewhere, which the wrap-up State block is not asked to cover.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `readState` gains a remote-ref fallback: when `@{u}` is unset, or resolves to a ref other than `origin/{branch}`, it checks `git rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options refs/remotes/origin/{branch}`; when that ref exists, `ahead`/`behind` are computed with `rev-list --left-right --count refs/remotes/origin/{branch}...HEAD` and `pushed` follows the same `ahead === 0` rule. The result carries a new `remoteRef` field (`'origin/{branch}'` or `null`) and a `pushedVia: 'upstream' | 'remote-ref' | null` field; `upstream` keeps reporting the configured `@{u}` (or `null`) unchanged.
- [ ] `render.js` distinguishes the three shapes: `pushed (origin/{branch}; no upstream configured)` when `pushedVia === 'remote-ref'`; the existing `pushed`/`UNPUSHED ({upstream})` lines when `pushedVia === 'upstream'`; `UNPUSHED (no upstream, origin/{branch} absent)` when neither ref exists. The unknown case (`pushed === null`) keeps its current wording.
- [ ] `bin/wrap-up-state.js`'s reflog read uses `state.remoteRef` when `state.upstream` is null, so the concatenated-reflog logic sees the remote-tracking ref's updates too.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/state.test.js` (fake-runner style, beside the three existing `pushed` cases): no upstream + remote ref present + ahead 0 → `pushed: true`, `pushedVia: 'remote-ref'`; no upstream + remote ref present + ahead 2 → `pushed: false`; no upstream + no remote ref → `pushed: false`, `remoteRef: null`; inherited upstream (`origin/main`) + remote ref present → judged by the remote ref, not `@{u}`; existing cases unchanged. `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/render.test.js` pins the three rendered lines.
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/` line (the family-1 sentence that says `state.js` reads branch/upstream/ahead-behind/pushed facts) names the remote-ref fallback in one clause.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. On a branch pushed with `git push origin {branch}` and no upstream configured, `node bin/wrap-up-state.js --since <base>` renders a `pushed` line naming `origin/{branch}`; after one more local commit it renders `UNPUSHED` with the ahead count.
2. On a branch whose `@{u}` is the inherited `origin/main` (the #1860 shape) but whose `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` matches HEAD, the line reads pushed, not `UNPUSHED (origin/main)`.
3. A branch that was never pushed still renders UNPUSHED, and a failed `rev-list` read under either ref still yields `pushed: null` (unknown), never a definite false.
4. All existing `state.test.js` and `render.test.js` cases pass unmodified; `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Helper-side fallback rather than `-u` on the lifecycle's first push: the fallback fixes the State block for branches pushed by any tool (the record's own second point), needs no change to the three skill files that spell the push command, and does not interact with `hasNoUpstreamYet` in `pre-tool-use.js`, which since #1860 already reads `@{u}` vs `origin/{branch}` and would need re-verification if the lifecycle started setting upstreams. The `--end-of-options` separator before the ref follows the repo's `git` argument rule (#1686's citation).

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/state.js` — `readState` (the `@{u}` read, `ahead`/`behind`, the `pushed` rule and its comment).
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/render.js` — the `UNPUSHED (no upstream)` line and its siblings.
- `plugin/bin/wrap-up-state.js` — `state.upstream` reflog selection.
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/state.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/render.test.js` — fake-runner fixtures.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`, `plugin/skills/_shared/git-discipline.md` — read-only: the push form that leaves `@{u}` unset.

## Gotchas
- `git branch --show-current` returns empty on a detached HEAD; the fallback must skip the remote-ref probe when `branch` is null, keeping today's detached-HEAD output.
- A remote named anything other than `origin` is out of scope; the lifecycle pushes to `origin` by contract (`_shared/integration-branch.md`), so hard-code it and say so in the comment rather than parsing `branch.{name}.remote`.
- The ordering rule stays: `pushed` is judged against whichever ref was chosen, never against both; a configured upstream that equals `origin/{branch}` takes precedence and the fallback is not consulted.
- `pushedVia` is additive on the JSON shape `--json` emits (#1930); no existing consumer reads the new field, so the shape change is backward compatible.

## Original request
**Summary:** `wrap-up-state.js --since <base>` rendered `Branch <branch> — 12 commits, UNPUSHED (no upstream)` for a branch whose every commit was already on `origin` (the phase-exit push had just printed `<old>..<new> <branch> -> <branch>`). The pr-first lifecycle pushes with `git push origin {branch}` — never `-u` — so `@{u}` is unset on every pr-first run and the helper's "pushed" judgment is wrong for exactly the runs whose State block the wrap-up summary is told to render verbatim.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/wrap-up-state.js` (push-status derivation), with `skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` Step 2 / `skills/_shared/git-discipline.md`'s phase-exit push as the reason `@{u}` is never set

**Cost this session:** one manual `git branch --set-upstream-to` to make the State block truthful, plus a Verdict line that had to be written from the push output instead of the helper — the opposite of what `summary-template.md` asks for ("never assert it landed from memory").

**Repro steps:**
1. Run any pr-first pipeline (draft PR opened at run start; phases push with `git push origin {branch}`).
2. At wrap-up, run `node bin/wrap-up-state.js --since <merge-base>`.
3. Observe `UNPUSHED (no upstream)` while `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/{branch}` returns the current HEAD sha.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: when `@{u}` is unset, the helper falls back to `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` (after the fetch it already does, or via `git ls-remote`) and reports pushed/unpushed from that; or the pr-early lifecycle's first push sets the upstream (`-u`) so `@{u}` is meaningful for the rest of the run.
Actual: the helper reports UNPUSHED whenever no upstream is configured, regardless of what origin holds.

**Definition:** Clear — either fix (helper fallback or `-u` on the first push) makes the State block correct; the helper-side fallback also covers branches pushed by tools that never set upstream.

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review. Two independently-merged PRs each shipped their
own Jaccard-similarity tokenizer and threshold constant, with no shared source and no test
importing either exported constant — so a change to one can silently invalidate the other's
tests without either noticing:

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` (confirmed, line 17, #1980): `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN = 0.4`
  + `SUBSTANCE_STOP_WORDS` (line 22).
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js` (confirmed, line 24, #1944):
  `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.5` + `STOP_WORDS` (line 30).

A search of `tests/` for either constant name returns zero hits —
`tests/bin-lib/issues/near-duplicate.test.js:66` hardcodes "0.5" in a test name/reasoning
(`'title similarity below the default 0.5 threshold does not fire'`) instead of importing the
real constant.

## Deliverables

- Decide whether these two similarity checks are conceptually the same primitive (in which case
  consolidate into one shared tokenizer/threshold module both import) or genuinely distinct
  enough to justify separate constants (in which case document why, and have each test import
  its own module's real constant instead of hardcoding the value).
- Update `near-duplicate.test.js` to import `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` rather than
  hardcoding 0.5.

## Acceptance Criteria

No test hardcodes either threshold as a bare numeric literal; both are imported from their
source module.

## Technical Approach

Read both modules' full similarity-scoring logic (`coordination.js`'s substance-similarity check
and `near-duplicate.js`'s title-similarity check) to judge whether they're the same primitive
applied to different inputs (substance text vs. titles) or genuinely distinct enough to warrant
separate stop-word lists and thresholds — this is the actual judgment call the Deliverables ask
for, not a mechanical decision this shaping pass can make without reading both algorithms'
full bodies. If consolidating: extract a shared tokenizer/stop-word/threshold module both import,
preserving each call site's own threshold value unless the investigation finds a reason to unify
those too. If keeping them separate: add a one-line comment at each constant's definition site
stating why the two are conceptually distinct, and fix the test regardless — the test-hardcoding
fix (Deliverable 2) applies either way. Update `near-duplicate.test.js:66` to import
`DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` and interpolate it into the test name/assertion instead of
the bare literal `0.5`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` — `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN`/`SUBSTANCE_STOP_WORDS`, possible
  consolidation target
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js` — `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD`/`STOP_WORDS`,
  possible consolidation target
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/near-duplicate.test.js` (line 66) — fix the hardcoded `0.5`

## Gotchas

- Per a standing memory in this codebase, similarity scores are normalization-sensitive —
  consolidating the two tokenizers is only safe if their actual normalization behavior (case
  folding, punctuation handling, stop-word removal order) genuinely matches; verify with a
  substitution+diff test before assuming they're interchangeable, not just by reading the
  constant values.
- If consolidating, do not silently change either module's effective threshold — a Jaccard
  score computed by a merged tokenizer can differ from the original even at the "same" nominal
  threshold value if the tokenization itself changes; re-verify both modules' existing test
  suites still pass with real (not just literal-matching) behavior preserved.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js`
— all three confirmed still true at this shaping pass:

- **Read-back race** (~line 400): post-write verification (#2073) re-reads immediately with no
  retry/backoff (`if (!verifyClaimLanded(deps, repoSlug, issue, opts.runId, knownTip))`). On the
  contents-API transport `knownTip` is `null`, so the read-back hits GitHub's
  eventually-consistent contents API and can legitimately return the pre-write blob — a spurious
  exit 5 on a claim that actually landed. The file's own header already warns against
  eventually-consistent GitHub reads elsewhere.
- **Claim leak on abort** (~line 227, confirmed): `abort()` releases only `claimedThisRun`
  (`releaseClaimedThisRun(deps, repoSlug, opts.runId, claimedThisRun)`). `stopOrSkip(issue,
  'unverified', 'unverified', 5, {})` runs (confirmed, ~line 401) *before* the target is pushed
  onto `claimedThisRun` (the `claimedThisRun.push(issue)` call is one line after the verification
  check), so a target whose claim genuinely landed (just couldn't be verified back) leaks until
  TTL expiry with no `bot:in-progress` marker making it visible.
- **Stale doc comment** (~line 225, confirmed): `abort()`'s comment still enumerates only exit
  codes 3 and 4 ("`exitCode` is 3 for a `contested`/`inFlight` envelope, 4 for a `transient`
  one") — exit 5 (`unverified`) was added without updating it.

## Deliverables

- Add a bounded retry/backoff to the post-write read-back verification when `knownTip` is `null`,
  before declaring exit 5.
- Release (or otherwise make visible) the `unverified` target's claim on abort, not just
  `claimedThisRun`.
- Update `abort()`'s doc comment to include exit 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A simulated eventually-consistent stale read on the contents-API path no longer produces a
  spurious exit 5 within the retry window.
- An aborted run with an `unverified` target leaves that claim in a state a later run can
  detect/reclaim before TTL, not silently leaked.
- `abort()`'s doc comment lists exit codes 3, 4, and 5.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

For the read-back race: wrap the `verifyClaimLanded` call (~line 400) in a small bounded
retry loop (a few attempts with a short backoff) specifically for the `knownTip === null` case —
the git-CAS path (`knownTip` set) already has a real tip to compare against and doesn't need
this, since a git-CAS success is immediately consistent. Only declare exit 5 after the retry
window is exhausted. For the claim leak: capture the `unverified` issue's claim state (the
context `verifyClaimLanded` already had before failing) and pass it to `abort()` so it can be
released or explicitly flagged alongside `claimedThisRun`'s own release — the goal is that a
genuinely-landed-but-unverified claim doesn't sit invisible until TTL; releasing it (so a later
run can pick it up cleanly) is the safer default over leaving it silently held. Update the
`abort()` doc comment in the same change.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js` — the read-back retry (~line 400), the claim
  leak fix (~line 227, `abort()` and the `unverified` stop path), and the doc comment update

## Gotchas

- The retry must be scoped to the `knownTip === null` (contents-API) path only — the git-CAS
  path's `knownTip`-based verification is already immediately consistent and doesn't need
  (or benefit from) a retry; adding one there would just slow down every claim for no
  correctness gain.
- Releasing an `unverified` claim on abort must not race with the claim that write actually
  produced — verify the release targets the same claim identity (`repoSlug`, `issue`, `opts.runId`)
  the write itself used, so a genuinely different run's claim on the same issue is never touched.

Surface: infra

## Current State

The `bot:parked` facet (merge-verification gate parked a record; grants stay intact —
`_shared/work-record.md`) was added, but several sites that classify or render bot state were
never updated to consult it, discovered during a pre-release whole-branch review — all confirmed
still true at this shaping pass:

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/backlog.js`'s `classifyBuckets` (~line 208): a parked record with grants
  intact still lands in `dispatchable` (confirmed: the if/else chain checks `f.bot.inProgress`,
  `f.stage === 'parked'`, `f.notPlanned`, `f.isParentIssue` — never `f.bot.parked` — before
  falling through to the `ready && granted` → `dispatchable` branch), so `/backlog overview`
  recommends `/dispatch`-ing a record that `/dispatch` itself refuses (contrast
  `queue-pull-script.md:115`, which does filter `!i.facets.bot.parked`).
- `plugin/bin/lib/record-graph/encode.js`'s `borderStyleFor` (~line 55, confirmed): only checks
  `bot.blocked`/`bot.inProgress`, so a parked record renders identically to a healthy one in
  `/visualize`'s queue diagram.
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-buckets.js`'s `isBotParked` (~line 22): exported but has zero
  callers anywhere in `plugin/bin/**` (confirmed by grep) — only skill prose
  (`tidy/step-1-records.md:164`) references it, so no JS path actually enforces the new bucket.
- `plugin/skills/backlog/attention-mode.md` (~line 69): the needs-you list filters on
  `bot:blocked` only — a merge-verification-parked record surfaces nowhere in `/backlog
  attention`.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md` (lines ~47, 149, 275) and `help/context-flow.md:67`:
  queue-exclusion prose names only `bot:blocked`, though `queue-pull-script.md` itself also
  excludes `bot:parked`.

## Deliverables

- `classifyBuckets` excludes `bot.parked` records from `dispatchable` (or buckets them
  separately).
- `borderStyleFor` returns a distinct style for `bot.parked`.
- `isBotParked` gets a real JS caller, or is removed if genuinely unneeded.
- `attention-mode.md` and the dispatch/help prose name `bot:parked` alongside `bot:blocked`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record with `bot:parked` and intact `auto:*` grants no longer appears in `/backlog
  overview`'s `dispatchable` bucket.
- `/visualize`'s queue diagram renders a parked record with a distinct border style.
- `/backlog attention` surfaces a parked record.
- `isBotParked` (`record-buckets.js`) has at least one real JS caller after this fix, or is
  removed from the module's exports with its prose reference (`tidy/step-1-records.md:164`)
  updated to not imply a JS enforcement path that doesn't exist.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Five independent, narrow edits, each following an existing sibling pattern already in the
codebase:

1. `backlog.js`'s `classifyBuckets` (~line 208): add a `f.bot.parked` check to the if/else chain,
   before the `ready && granted` branches — likely its own bucket (e.g. `buckets.parked` if one
   doesn't already exist for this exact case) rather than silently folding into an existing one,
   mirroring how `f.stage === 'parked'` already gets its own `buckets.parked` line just above.
2. `encode.js`'s `borderStyleFor` (~line 55): add a `bot.parked` branch returning a distinct
   style string, following the same `if (bot.blocked) return 'blocked'` pattern already there.
3. `record-buckets.js`'s `isBotParked`: wire it into `classifyBuckets` (step 1) as the real JS
   caller — this may make it redundant with a direct `f.bot.parked` check, so decide whether to
   call the predicate function or inline the check, whichever matches this file's existing
   style for its sibling predicates (`isBotBlocked` etc.).
4. `attention-mode.md` (~line 69): extend the needs-you filter to include `bot:parked` alongside
   `bot:blocked`.
5. `dispatch/SKILL.md` (~lines 47, 149, 275) and `help/context-flow.md:67`: update
   queue-exclusion prose to name `bot:parked` alongside `bot:blocked`, matching what
   `queue-pull-script.md` already does in code.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/backlog.js` — `classifyBuckets`, exclude/bucket `bot.parked`
- `plugin/bin/lib/record-graph/encode.js` — `borderStyleFor`, distinct style for `bot.parked`
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-buckets.js` — `isBotParked`, wire in a real caller or remove
- `plugin/skills/backlog/attention-mode.md` — needs-you filter, add `bot:parked`
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md` — queue-exclusion prose, name `bot:parked`
- `plugin/skills/help/context-flow.md` — queue-exclusion prose, name `bot:parked`
- `plugin/skills/tidy/step-1-records.md` — update if `isBotParked` usage changes

## Gotchas

- `bot:parked` records keep their `auto:*` grants intact by design (a merge-verification park is
  not a build failure, unlike `bot:blocked`) — the fix must exclude them from `dispatchable`
  without stripping or otherwise touching their grants.
- Don't conflate `bot:parked` with the pre-existing `stage === 'parked'` bucket in
  `classifyBuckets` — they're different concepts (a human-deferred backlog record vs. a
  merge-verification-parked ready record) and already have separate handling elsewhere; give
  `bot:parked` its own branch rather than merging it into the existing `parked` stage bucket.

# Backlog proposal — `0.x` pre-major bump rule in the pack and the local engine (#2256, ledger row 102)

**Category:** backlog-proposal
**Severity:** medium
**Reversibility:** high
**Source:** `/review` whole-branch review of #2256 (minor M7), confirmed by the release skill's own gate
**Defer-reason:** pre-existing-outside-diff
**Proposed title:** Honour release-please's `bump-minor-pre-major` — a breaking commit on a `0.x` line bumps the minor, not the major

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/release-local/bump.js` maps any breaking marker to `major`, and `plugin/bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js`'s `proposedVersion` reuses that rule (via `bin/lib/release/compose.js`). release-please, by default (`bump-minor-pre-major: true` behaviour on `0.x`), does not bump `0.x` to `1.0.0` on a breaking change. On a `0.x` pr-first repository the console therefore renders a major and `/claude-tweaks:release`'s major-bump HARD-GATE holds a release that release-please would ship as `0.(x+1).0`; the console's gating version and the engine's shipped version then disagree on every breaking change.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `bump.js`: when the base is `0.x`, a breaking marker yields `minor` (and a `feat` yields `patch` when `bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major` is set) — read from `release-please-config.json` when present, default `true`
- [ ] `pack.js`'s `proposedVersion` carries `part` computed by the same rule, and its `value` names `preMajor: true` so the console can say why
- [ ] `release/console.md`'s major-bump gate reads `proposedVersion.value.part`, not a recomputation; tests in `tests/bin-lib/release-local/bump.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/release-preflight/pack.test.js`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Base `0.4.2` + a `feat!:` commit → `bump.js` proposes `0.5.0`; base `1.4.2` + the same → `2.0.0`.
2. The pack on a `0.x` fixture with a breaking commit reports `part: minor`, `preMajor: true`.
3. `/claude-tweaks:release --dry-run` on that fixture renders no major-bump HARD-GATE.


---

# Backlog proposal — `--release-as` on the local engine (#2256, ledger row 90)

**Category:** backlog-proposal
**Severity:** low
**Reversibility:** high
**Source:** `/release` Step 5 gap surfaced at #2256's plan phase; `/wrap-up` Phase 3 SETTLE
**Defer-reason:** genuinely-larger
**Proposed title:** Add `--release-as <version>` to `bin/release-local.js` so `/claude-tweaks:release --as` works under local-merge

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:release --as <version>` is pr-first only: it pushes a `Release-As:` commit that release-please re-renders. Under `local-merge` the engine (`plugin/bin/release-local.js`, #2254) derives the version from first-parent conventional history (`bin/lib/release-local/bump.js`) and has no override, so the skill refuses `--as` right after Step 1 with `--as is pr-first only (release-local.js derives the version from history); use a breaking commit or a manual tag` (SKILL.md Input table, ruling 17).

## Deliverables

- [ ] `bin/release-local.js --release-as <version>` (strict `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`), threaded into `bin/lib/release/precheck.js` as an explicit candidate that must be ahead of the version base, and into the manifest/CHANGELOG writers as the version to splice
- [ ] `/claude-tweaks:release` Step 1's refusal replaced by passing `--release-as {version}` under local-merge; the Input table row and `execute.md`'s back-stop updated; ledger row 90 closed
- [ ] Tests in `tests/bin-lib/release-local/` (accepted ahead-of-base value; rejected behind/equal value; dry-run plan line naming the override)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `release-local.js --dry-run --release-as 7.0.0` on a minor-only history plans `v7.0.0` and names the override in its plan line.
2. `--release-as 1.0.0` when the base is `1.2.0` exits `2` with a usage-shaped message naming both versions.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Issue #1882 (splitFrontmatterFence returns null on every CRLF checkout) is closed, and the PR
that closed it (#2035) shows as merged — but the merge only carries commit 92a6ff1a,
"Materialize spec for #1882," which added `work/1882-spec.md` (49 lines). The actual code fix
was never committed to that PR.

Sequence of events: a `/claude-tweaks:dispatch next` firing selected #1882 and dispatched a
build,test Task agent. That agent wrote the real fix (`content.split('\n')` -> `content.split(/\r?\n/)`
in `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.js`) plus two CRLF-fixture regression tests, but
had not yet committed them when the session's container was reclaimed for inactivity mid-run. The
pipeline run (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-07T121938-record-1882`) was left parked with
status `interrupted`. Five days later the repo owner manually marked the still-draft PR #2035
ready for review and merged it directly, without the automated test/review/wrap-up phases ever
running (the PR body's phases checklist — build/test/review/wrap-up — was still fully unchecked
at merge time). GitHub auto-closed #1882 via the PR's "Fixes #1882" line.

**Confirmed still true at this shaping pass:** `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.js:35`
still reads `content.split('\n')` on `origin/main` — the CRLF bug is still live, affecting all
six call sites #1882 originally listed (skill-audit description/argument-hint measurement,
journey/harness/docs-health scope fields, and `work-backend: local-files` record frontmatter
parsing). The orphaned fix branch `worktree-record-1882` still exists at commit `9a883f98`
(confirmed present on `origin`), 2 commits ahead of the merged PR's head 92a6ff1a: `6ec86bd5`
(the actual fix + 2 regression tests) and `9a883f98` (an implementation plan doc). No new PR for
#1882 has been opened since this record was filed (confirmed: `gh pr list --search "1882"`
returns none open).

Separately, this points at a process gap: `integration-model: pr-first` has no safeguard today
against a human merging a draft PR before the automated build/test/review/wrap-up phases push
their commits — the phases checklist showing all-unchecked at merge time was a visible signal
that went unheeded.

## Deliverables

- Land the actual fix: open a PR from branch `worktree-record-1882` (or cherry-pick commits
  `6ec86bd5` and `9a883f98` onto a fresh branch) against `main`, verify CI, and merge it.
- Decide whether to add a safeguard (e.g. a merge-time check, or a documented process rule)
  against merging a `pr-first` draft PR whose phases checklist isn't fully checked — implement
  one if it's judged worthwhile, or explicitly decline with recorded reasoning if not.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.js`'s `splitFrontmatterFence` uses
   `content.split(/\r?\n/)` on `main`.
2. `tests/bin-lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.test.js` carries the two CRLF-fixture regression
   tests on `main`, passing.
3. The premature-merge process gap is either addressed (a concrete safeguard implemented) or
   explicitly declined with reasoning recorded in this record's closing comment.
4. `npm test` passes on `main` after the fix lands.

## Technical Approach

Cherry-pick (or PR directly from) branch `worktree-record-1882` at commit `9a883f98` — the fix
commit `6ec86bd5` plus the implementation-plan-doc commit `9a883f98` — onto a fresh branch off
current `main`, resolving any merge drift from the five days of intervening main history. Open a
PR, let CI run for real (this time), and merge through the normal pipeline rather than a manual
merge — the exact process failure this record exists to correct. For the safeguard deliverable,
survey what mechanism this repo already has for gating merges (`_shared/pr-first-merge.md`'s
existing merge-verification gate, Claude Approvals rules if in use) and judge whether adding a
phases-checklist check there is proportionate, or whether the existing safeguards are deemed
sufficient and this was a one-off human override that no mechanism should have blocked.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.js` — apply the CRLF-safe split (already written
  on the orphaned branch; land it)
- `tests/bin-lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.test.js` — the two CRLF regression tests (already
  written on the orphaned branch; land them)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge.md` — reference for whatever existing merge-gating
  mechanism the safeguard deliverable might extend
- `specs/2-pr-2035-merged-only-the-spec-materialization-commit-1882-s-a.md` — a duplicate local
  unsynced record from the same incident (see Gotchas); do not re-file, this GitHub issue is the
  canonical record per the original filer's own note

## Gotchas

- Do not reopen #2035 or open a competing PR under a different framing — the original filer
  explicitly followed a standing instruction not to reopen #2035 or open a new PR "without being
  asked"; this record's own Deliverables now constitute that ask, so proceeding is expected, not
  a violation of that instruction.
- A duplicate local record exists (`specs/2-pr-2035-merged-only-the-spec-materialization-commit-1882-s-a.md`,
  on branch `worktree-capture-1882-followup`) from the same investigation, filed when `gh` was
  unavailable — this GitHub issue is the canonical record per the original filer's own note; the
  local file is paper trail only and should not be independently actioned.
- Verify the cherry-picked fix still applies cleanly given five days of intervening `main` history
  before assuming a straight cherry-pick works — check for conflicts in
  `frontmatter-list.js` or its test file first.

## Original request

## Current State

Issue #1882 (splitFrontmatterFence returns null on every CRLF checkout) is closed, and the PR that closed it (#2035) shows as merged — but the merge only carries commit 92a6ff1a, "Materialize spec for #1882", which added `work/1882-spec.md` (49 lines). The actual code fix was never committed to that PR.

Sequence of events: a `/claude-tweaks:dispatch next` firing selected #1882 and dispatched a build,test Task agent. That agent wrote the real fix (`content.split('\n')` -> `content.split(/\r?\n/)` in `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.js`) plus two CRLF-fixture regression tests, but had not yet committed them when the session's container was reclaimed for inactivity mid-run. The pipeline run (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-07T121938-record-1882`) was left parked with status `interrupted`. Five days later the repo owner manually marked the still-draft PR #2035 ready for review and merged it directly, without the automated test/review/wrap-up phases ever running (the PR body's phases checklist — build/test/review/wrap-up — was still fully unchecked at merge time). GitHub auto-closed #1882 via the PR's "Fixes #1882" line.

Verified directly against `origin/main`: `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.js` still contains the buggy `content.split('\n')` line (`git show origin/main:plugin/bin/lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.js`). The CRLF bug is still live on main, affecting all six call sites #1882 originally listed (skill-audit description/argument-hint measurement, journey/harness/docs-health scope fields, and `work-backend: local-files` record frontmatter parsing).

The orphaned fix has been recovered and preserved: pushed to branch `worktree-record-1882` at commit 9a883f98 (2 commits ahead of the merged PR's head 92a6ff1a): `6ec86bd5` (the actual fix + 2 regression tests) and `9a883f98` (the implementation plan doc). `node --test tests/bin-lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.test.js` passes all 14 tests on that branch, including the 2 new CRLF regression tests. Per the standing instruction not to reopen #2035 or open a new PR for the same change without being asked, no new PR was opened.

Separately, this points at a process gap: `integration-model: pr-first` has no safeguard today against a human merging a draft PR before the automated build/test/review/wrap-up phases push their commits — the phases checklist showing all-unchecked at merge time was a visible signal that went unheeded.

Also filed as a local unsynced record (`specs/2-pr-2035-merged-only-the-spec-materialization-commit-1882-s-a.md`, pushed on branch `worktree-capture-1882-followup`) since `gh` CLI was unavailable in the session that first investigated this — kept for paper trail; this issue is now the canonical record.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Open a PR from branch `worktree-record-1882` (or cherry-pick commits `6ec86bd5` and `9a883f98` onto a fresh branch) against `main`, verify CI, and merge it so the actual fix lands
- [ ] Decide whether to add a safeguard (e.g. a merge-time check, or a Claude Approvals rule) against merging a `pr-first` draft PR whose phases checklist isn't fully checked

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.js`'s `splitFrontmatterFence` uses `content.split(/\r?\n/)` on `main`
2. `tests/bin-lib/health-core/frontmatter-list.test.js` carries the two CRLF-fixture regression tests on `main`, passing
3. The premature-merge process gap is either addressed or explicitly declined with reasoning recorded
