## Current State

Reconcile's automated hygiene sweep flags this pipeline run directory as `structurally-stuck` (`reason: no-branch`), auto-filing this issue per `bin/lib/reconcile`'s escalation mechanism (#644 Deliverable 2 / #1613's visibility layer).

The stuck directory: `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-05T094933-record-733`. Its `run-state.json` stamps `worktree: .claude/worktrees/dispatch-record-733` and `pr: {number: 1891, branch: worktree-dispatch-record-733}`.

Investigation confirms the underlying work already shipped cleanly: issue #733 is closed, PR #1891 merged 2026-09-05T19:08:37Z, and both the worktree and the `worktree-dispatch-record-733` branch have since been deleted (`git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/worktree-dispatch-record-733` confirms it no longer exists locally) — there is nothing left to build or resolve; the run directory is legitimately done and should have been archived.

This is the same root cause tracked in #2226 (a sibling `reconcile: structurally-stuck` record, filed against a different directory): `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `#1962` no-branch fallback probes the PR by number via `resolvePrStateByNumber` when the stamped worktree and its branch are both gone, but only archives when `byNumber.state === 'CLOSED'` — a closed-without-merging PR. A PR that was actually merged reports `state: 'MERGED'`, which this check never matches, so a merged-then-cleaned-up run permanently falls through to the plain `no-branch` skip on every pass — exactly the symptom this issue reports.

## Deliverables

- Fix belongs with #2226, which already deliverables the code change for this exact root cause: extend `archive-merged.js`'s `#1962` fallback to also recognize `byNumber.state === 'MERGED'`, gated by `localHasMerge(root, byNumber.mergeCommit)` (see #2226 for the full deliverable). This record names an eighth independent instance of the same bug (alongside #2226, #2229, #2354-#2358).
- Once #2226's fix lands, resolve this specific stuck directory (`2026-09-05T094933-record-733`) so this issue's own escalation clears.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-05T094933-record-733` is archived (or otherwise resolved) and no longer reported `structurally-stuck` by reconcile.
- [ ] Confirmed this directory's stuck state is resolved by #2226's fix landing — if investigation at build time finds a *different* mechanism for this specific directory, treat that as new information and re-diagnose rather than assuming #2226's fix covers it.

## Technical Approach

No new code investigation needed here beyond confirming #2226's fix (once it lands) actually resolves this directory too — same `no-branch` + merged-and-deleted-branch pattern. See #2226's Technical Approach for the code-level fix.

### Key Files

- `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — same file, same `#1962` fallback block #2226 fixes; no additional change expected here

## Gotchas

- This is one of several `reconcile: structurally-stuck` auto-filed issues sharing the same underlying `#1962`-fallback gap (see also #2226, #2228, #2229, #2230, #2231, #2354-#2358). #2226 carries the actual code fix for the MERGED-state gap; #2228 carries a second, independent gap in the same block. Once both land, re-check every sibling `structurally-stuck` issue rather than resolving each one's directory by hand — a human should also confirm whether #1811 (an earlier, already-`ready`, more comprehensive consolidated fix for this same defect family, discovered during this shaping pass) already supersedes some or all of these.
- The near-duplicate screen does not flag these reconcile-residue records against each other by design (title-similarity is deliberately excluded for `reconcile:`-prefixed titles) — this cross-reference is a manual note, not an automated signal.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `resolveParent()` (line 392) resolves a record's decomposition parent with `gh issue view {n} --json parent`. On `gh` 2.92.0 (2026-04-28) that field is not in the command's JSON field list, the call throws `Unknown JSON field: "parent"`, and `resolveParent` returns `{ok: false}` — which the `acceptance-labeling` check folds into a `fail` row, so `wrap-up-engine.js verify` exits 3 and `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s Verify step withholds the closure line (`execution-and-verification.md`'s exit-3 rule) on every record-mode run, even when the record's `demo:*` labeling is correct. On `gh` 2.96.0 (this checkout, 2026-09-09) the same command returns `{"parent": null}`, so the failure is version-dependent: any sandbox or machine still on 2.92.x hits it on every run.

Two things are wrong at once. The field choice is fragile — the plugin's other parent/sub-issue resolution (`bin/lib/issues/native-dependencies.js`, `fetchNativeSubIssues`) goes through GraphQL, which exposes `Issue.parent` on every `gh` version that can run GraphQL at all. And the failure class is misreported — every other gather failure in this file (`git status`, `git worktree list`, `git log`, `gh pr view`, lines 172–326) renders `result: 'unknown'`, which the closure line quotes without blocking, while `resolveParent`'s failure alone is rendered as `fail`, turning a tooling gap into a false labeling verdict.

## Deliverables

- Resolve the parent through GraphQL — `gh api graphql` with `repository(owner,name){ issue(number){ parent { number } } }` — through the same `deps.gh` seam the rest of the file uses, so the test double can drive it; keep the resolution in `resolveParent` (or a sibling in `native-dependencies.js` it delegates to) and drop the `--json parent` call.
- When the parent gather itself fails (GraphQL error, unparseable response), render the `acceptance-labeling` row as `result: 'unknown'` with the gather error in `detail`, matching the file's other could-not-gather rows — never `fail`. **Related:** #2354, #2355, #2356, #2357, #2359

Surface: infra

## Current State

Reconcile's automated hygiene sweep flags this pipeline run directory as `structurally-stuck` (`reason: no-branch`), auto-filing this issue per `bin/lib/reconcile`'s escalation mechanism (#644 Deliverable 2 / #1613's visibility layer).

The stuck directory: `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-05T145253-record-1580`. Its `run-state.json` stamps `worktree: .claude/worktrees/dispatch-record-1580` and `pr: {number: 1907, branch: worktree-dispatch-record-1580}`.

Investigation confirms the underlying work already shipped cleanly: issue #1580 is closed, PR #1907 merged 2026-09-05T19:08:34Z, and both the worktree and the `worktree-dispatch-record-1580` branch have since been deleted (`git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/worktree-dispatch-record-1580` confirms it no longer exists locally) — there is nothing left to build or resolve; the run directory is legitimately done and should have been archived.

This is the same root cause tracked in #2226 (a sibling `reconcile: structurally-stuck` record, filed against a different directory): `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `#1962` no-branch fallback probes the PR by number via `resolvePrStateByNumber` when the stamped worktree and its branch are both gone, but only archives when `byNumber.state === 'CLOSED'` — a closed-without-merging PR. A PR that was actually merged reports `state: 'MERGED'`, which this check never matches, so a merged-then-cleaned-up run permanently falls through to the plain `no-branch` skip on every pass — exactly the symptom this issue reports.

## Deliverables

- Fix belongs with #2226, which already deliverables the code change for this exact root cause: extend `archive-merged.js`'s `#1962` fallback to also recognize `byNumber.state === 'MERGED'`, gated by `localHasMerge(root, byNumber.mergeCommit)` (see #2226 for the full deliverable). This record names a seventh independent instance of the same bug (alongside #2226, #2229, #2354, #2355, #2356, #2357).
- Once #2226's fix lands, resolve this specific stuck directory (`2026-09-05T145253-record-1580`) so this issue's own escalation clears.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-05T145253-record-1580` is archived (or otherwise resolved) and no longer reported `structurally-stuck` by reconcile.
- [ ] Confirmed this directory's stuck state is resolved by #2226's fix landing — if investigation at build time finds a *different* mechanism for this specific directory, treat that as new information and re-diagnose rather than assuming #2226's fix covers it.

## Technical Approach

No new code investigation needed here beyond confirming #2226's fix (once it lands) actually resolves this directory too — same `no-branch` + merged-and-deleted-branch pattern. See #2226's Technical Approach for the code-level fix.

### Key Files

- `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — same file, same `#1962` fallback block #2226 fixes; no additional change expected here

## Gotchas

- This is one of several `reconcile: structurally-stuck` auto-filed issues sharing the same underlying `#1962`-fallback gap (see also #2226, #2228, #2229, #2230, #2231, #2354-#2357, #2359). #2226 carries the actual code fix for the MERGED-state gap; #2228 carries a second, independent gap in the same block. Once both land, re-check every sibling `structurally-stuck` issue rather than resolving each one's directory by hand — a human should also confirm whether #1811 (an earlier, already-`ready`, more comprehensive consolidated fix for this same defect family, discovered during this shaping pass) already supersedes some or all of these.
- The near-duplicate screen does not flag these reconcile-residue records against each other by design (title-similarity is deliberately excluded for `reconcile:`-prefixed titles) — this cross-reference is a manual note, not an automated signal.

## Current State
`recordLabels` (`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js:393-400`) loops sequentially over `inputs.records`, `await`ing one `gh issue view {n} --json labels` call per record, instead of running the independent per-record calls concurrently via `Promise.all` — `pack.js` already uses `Promise.all` elsewhere in the module (line 452, over its top-level probe set). A multi-record flow run with N=4-5 backlog records pays N sequential gh round-trips (network latency, ~300-800ms each) instead of running concurrently, adding seconds of unnecessary wall-clock time to the wrap-up fact pack that gates release.

`ghReadGrants` (`plugin/bin/console-resolve.js:73-84`, not `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` as originally cited — that file only *consumes* it via the `readGrants` dependency) is a different shape: its per-record `execFile('gh', [...], {cwd})` calls are synchronous (`execFile` there defaults to `execFileSync`-based `defaultExecFile`, line 51), not `await`ed promises. `readSnapshot` (`plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js:120-138`) calls `deps.readGrants(members)` synchronously inside a plain `try/catch` and `resolveAll` (`resolve.js:292`) itself is not `async`. Converting `ghReadGrants` to `Promise.all` would require first converting its `execFile` primitive to an async form, then threading `async`/`await` through `readSnapshot`, `resolveAll`, and `console-resolve.js`'s own `run()` — a materially larger, structurally invasive change to a file whose header comment says it deliberately "resolve[s] ... in one process," not a drop-in loop conversion. That part of the original request doesn't hold as scoped and is left out of this record's deliverables.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Convert `recordLabels`'s `for (const n of inputs.records) { await gh(...) }` loop (`pack.js:393-400`) to `Promise.all(inputs.records.map(async (n) => { ... }))`, preserving the `{[n]: labels[]}` output shape.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `recordLabels` issues its per-record `gh` calls concurrently.
2. No behavioral change to the returned data shape (`{[recordNumber]: string[]}`) or error handling (a rejected call still surfaces the same way it does today).
3. Existing `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js` `recordLabels` assertions (lines 122-123, 139, 221, 318-321, 326-329, 425-426) pass unchanged.

## Technical Approach
Mirror the existing `Promise.all` idiom already used in this file (`pack.js:452`) rather than introducing a new pattern.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `recordLabels` (line 393)
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js` — existing `recordLabels` coverage to keep green

## Gotchas
- `ghReadGrants` (`plugin/bin/console-resolve.js:73`) is out of scope for this record: it's exec-synchronous, not async/await, and its result is consumed synchronously by `resolveAll`/`readSnapshot` — converting it would ripple through the whole console-resolve call chain, a separate and larger-scoped change than "convert a loop."
- `claim` (`pack.js`, a few lines below `recordLabels`) has the identical sequential-loop shape and is not part of this record's scope either — the original request named only `recordLabels` and `ghReadGrants`.

## Original request
Found by the pre-v6.119.0 whole-branch review (range e7d6d9331..4db32e020).

Surface: infra

## Current State

`tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js` (added for #2030) scans build/test/review/design-wrapper/wrap-up/flow/`_shared` for real nested `/claude-tweaks:{name}` Skill-tool invocations and asserts each is either a `PHASES` member, a `plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` `NESTED_PARENT` key, or an allowlisted descriptive-only mention. The scan found three genuine nested invocations that are none of those:

- `plugin/skills/flow/SKILL.md:80` — "Run `/claude-tweaks:stories` with the detected URL" (flow's automatic story generation).
- `plugin/skills/flow/SKILL.md:195` / `plugin/skills/flow/survey.md:69` — "invoke `/claude-tweaks:deepen <changed-source-files>`" (flow's Depth Opportunities survey).
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md:126` / `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md:115` — "invoke `/claude-tweaks:feedback --pre-confirmed`" (Review Console upstream-feedback filing).

None of `stories`, `deepen`, `feedback` are in `NESTED_PARENT`, so a `skill_invoked` event for any of them currently opens its own new top-level phase row in `derive.js`'s output rather than nesting into the enclosing phase (`build`'s stories generation, `wrap-up`'s Review Console, etc.) — exactly the "spurious top-level phase" behavior `derive.js`'s own roster comment warns about. The conformance test (#2030) allowlists these three by name, with a pointer to this issue, rather than silently deciding the phase-attribution question itself.

**Resolved here** — all three follow the same pattern as `NESTED_PARENT`'s nine existing entries
(`simplify`, `reflect`, `visual-review`, `capture`, `design-wrapper`, `challenge`,
`assess-agent-autonomy`, `ledger`, `journeys`): each is a skill dispatched *as a sub-step* of a
larger pipeline skill's own procedure, never itself a top-level pipeline phase (`build`, `test`,
`review`, `polish`, `wrap-up`, `merge`). `stories` (flow's automatic story generation) is the
direct analogue of already-nested `journeys` (also a doc/artifact-generation sub-step of build).
`deepen` (flow's Depth Opportunities survey) is the direct analogue of already-nested `reflect`/
`simplify` (analysis passes run as pipeline sub-steps). `feedback` (Review Console's
upstream-feedback filing) is the direct analogue of already-nested `capture` (a filing action
invoked as a pipeline sub-step). None of the three is ever a user-facing standalone pipeline
stage the way `build`/`review`/`wrap-up` are.

## Deliverables

- Add `stories`, `deepen`, and `feedback` to `plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js`'s `NESTED_PARENT`
  map, each mapped to `'enclosing'` — matching the nine existing entries' shape exactly.
- Remove `stories`, `deepen`, and `feedback` from `tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js`'s
  allowlist (they're no longer an unresolved gap once they're `NESTED_PARENT` members).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js` no longer needs `deepen`/`stories`/`feedback` in
   its allowlist — they've moved to `NESTED_PARENT` instead.
2. A `skill_invoked` event for `stories`, `deepen`, or `feedback` nests into its enclosing phase
   in `derivePhases()`'s output rather than opening a new top-level phase — covered by a test
   case mirroring the existing `NESTED_PARENT` entries' own test coverage in
   `tests/bin-lib/timing/derive.test.js` (or wherever the existing nine entries are tested).
3. `npm test` stays green.

## Technical Approach

Add three entries to the existing `NESTED_PARENT` object literal in
`plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` (~line 21), each `'enclosing'` — the identical value every
existing entry already uses (`isTopLevel()` at line 55 only checks map membership, not the
value, so `'enclosing'` is the only value this map currently uses; keep it consistent). Then
remove the three names from `tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js`'s `ALLOWLIST` and add
(or extend) a test case asserting each nests correctly, following whatever pattern the existing
nine entries' own coverage already uses.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` — add three entries to `NESTED_PARENT` (~line 21)
- `tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js` — remove the three names from `ALLOWLIST`
- `tests/bin-lib/timing/derive.test.js` (or the actual location of `NESTED_PARENT`'s existing
  test coverage — verify at build time) — add coverage for the three new entries

## Gotchas

- This record resolves the phase-attribution question itself (all three nest) rather than
  leaving it open, based on direct structural analogy to `NESTED_PARENT`'s nine existing
  entries — every one of them is a sub-step skill invoked from within a larger pipeline
  procedure, exactly the shape `stories`/`deepen`/`feedback` share. If a maintainer disagrees
  that one of the three should nest, that's a five-minute label removal from the map, not a
  structural problem with this fix.
- Do not add a fourth, differently-shaped value to `NESTED_PARENT` (e.g. naming a *specific*
  parent phase) — every existing entry uses the literal string `'enclosing'`, and `isTopLevel()`
  only checks map membership, so introducing a new value shape would be unused complexity.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`agent-browser` is a third-party tool this plugin depends on optionally (CLAUDE.md's Dependencies
table) — it is not part of this repo's own codebase; `plugin/skills/browse/agent-browser-reference.md`
documents its usage but does not own its implementation. That reference file's documented operation
vocabulary (open, snapshot, find, click, fill, screenshot, vitals, trace, etc.) has no
color-scheme/emulation flag.

Verifying a light-mode-only CSS change in a project whose theming is driven solely by
`prefers-color-scheme` media queries (no in-app toggle) required building a standalone HTML
fixture with the target CSS rules copied in and the desired scheme's token values inlined, opened
via `file://`, instead of driving the live app in the actual scheme under test — a real but
indirect substitute.

Because `agent-browser` is external, this record's scope is bounded by what this repo can
actually change: whether the tool already supports color-scheme emulation through some mechanism
not yet documented here, and if not, formalizing the documented workaround so a future verifier
doesn't have to rediscover it.

## Deliverables

- Investigate whether the installed `agent-browser` version already supports color-scheme
  emulation via an undocumented flag, environment variable, or underlying CDP passthrough (e.g.
  `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`) — check its own `--help` output and any bundled documentation
  first.
- If a mechanism already exists: document it in `agent-browser-reference.md`'s operation
  vocabulary, with a usage example.
- If no mechanism exists: document the standalone-HTML-fixture workaround (build a minimal
  fixture with the target CSS and the desired scheme's token values inlined, open via `file://`)
  as the recommended pattern in `agent-browser-reference.md`, so a future verifier facing the same
  gap has a documented path instead of reinventing it — and, separately, file feedback against
  `agent-browser` itself (outside this repo) requesting the capability, since this repo cannot add
  a feature to a tool it doesn't own.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `agent-browser-reference.md` documents either (a) a working color-scheme emulation flag/option,
  verified against the actually-installed tool version, or (b) the standalone-fixture workaround
  pattern, clearly labeled as a workaround rather than a native capability.
- Whichever path is documented is validated by actually using it to verify a light-mode-only (or
  dark-mode-only) CSS change against a real project with `prefers-color-scheme`-only theming —
  not merely described in the abstract.
- If no native mechanism exists, upstream feedback is filed against `agent-browser` (outside this
  repo's own issue tracker) requesting the capability, and that filing is referenced from this
  record's closing comment.

## Technical Approach

Run `agent-browser --help` (and any subcommand-specific help, e.g. `agent-browser open --help`)
against the actually-installed version to check for an existing but undocumented emulation
option before assuming none exists — third-party tools frequently expose CDP-passthrough flags
that aren't surfaced in every doc surface. If nothing surfaces, formalize the fixture-based
workaround already used as a real substitute: a minimal standalone HTML file with the target
CSS rules and the desired scheme's computed token values inlined, opened via `agent-browser open
file://<path>`. Document whichever path is real in `agent-browser-reference.md`'s existing
operation-vocabulary section, in the same format as its other documented operations.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/browse/agent-browser-reference.md` — document the flag (if found) or the
  fixture-workaround pattern (if not)

## Gotchas

- `agent-browser` is a third-party dependency, not part of this repo's own codebase — this
  record cannot add a capability to the tool itself; it can only document what already exists or
  formalize a workaround, plus file upstream feedback if the capability is genuinely absent.
- Don't document a workaround as if it were a native capability — the Acceptance Criteria
  requires the documentation to be honest about which case applies.

## Original request

**Summary:** Verifying a light-mode-only CSS change in a project whose theming is driven solely by `prefers-color-scheme` media queries (no in-app toggle) required building a standalone HTML fixture instead of driving the live app, because agent-browser's documented operation vocabulary has no color-scheme/emulation flag.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** skills/browse (agent-browser-reference.md)

**Use case:** A project ships theming entirely via `prefers-color-scheme` with no manual toggle in the UI. Verifying a change scoped to the non-default color scheme (e.g. light mode when the OS/browser default is dark) requires driving the app in that scheme. `agent-browser`'s documented operation vocabulary (open, snapshot, find, click, fill, screenshot, vitals, trace, etc. per agent-browser-reference.md) has no color-scheme emulation option, so the only available workaround is building a standalone HTML fixture with the target CSS rules copied in and the desired scheme's token values inlined, then opening it via `file://` — a real but indirect substitute for driving the live app in the actual scheme under test.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.118.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js`.
The test named "no Key Files section and no title match can never classify strong" only asserts
`tier === 'weak'`; it never covers the module's stated "never upgrades a tier on missing data"
rule (confirmed, `shipped-candidate.js:27`'s comment: "a PR absent from this map is simply 'files
not fetched for it,' which the files-based strong signal treats the same as 'files don't cover
everything' — it never upgrades a tier on missing data"). No existing test supplies a record with
Key Files, no title match, and no `prFiles` entry at all — the actual missing-data path the
comment describes.

## Deliverables

Add a test case supplying a record with a Key Files section, no title match, and no `prFiles`
entry, asserting the module does not upgrade the tier on that missing data.

## Acceptance Criteria

The new test fails if the missing-data guard is removed from `shipped-candidate.js`, proving it
actually exercises the rule.

## Technical Approach

Add a test case to `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js`, alongside the existing "no
Key Files section and no title match can never classify strong" test, using a record that DOES
carry a `### Key Files` section (unlike the existing test) but whose corresponding PR number has
no entry in `opts.prFiles` — asserting the result stays `tier: 'weak'`, not `'strong'`, proving
the missing-`prFiles`-entry path is treated as "files don't cover everything" rather than
silently upgrading. Verify the test actually discriminates per the Acceptance Criteria: comment
out or bypass the missing-data guard in `shipped-candidate.js` locally and confirm the new test
fails, before considering it done.

### Key Files

- `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js` — add the missing-`prFiles`-entry test case
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js` (line ~27, read-only reference) — the rule being
  tested

## Gotchas

- The test must supply a record that genuinely has a `### Key Files` section (the existing
  no-Key-Files test doesn't exercise this path at all) — the distinguishing setup is Key Files
  present + no title match + no `prFiles` entry, not merely "no `prFiles` entry" alone.
- Per this record's own Acceptance Criteria, verify the test discriminates by temporarily
  removing the guard and confirming a failure — don't skip this verification step.

No existing test supplies a record with Key Files, no title match, and no prFiles entry at all — the actual missing-data path the comment describes.
